7	/// The port later epics extend (Code Map) — `features/capture/` depends on
8	/// this abstract class only, never `entries/data` or `entries/presentation`
9	/// (RNF06).
10	abstract class EntriesRepository {
11	  /// Posts to `entries-create` (`ApiClient.post`, via
12	  /// `EntriesRemoteDataSource`) and, on success, writes the entry through
13	  /// to the `entries` Hive box before returning `Right` (Boundaries) — a
14	  /// caller that only reads the returned [Entry] never needs to touch the
15	  /// box itself. Every [Failure] — including
16	  /// [Failure.networkOffline] — is returned as `Left`, unmapped and
17	  /// un-retried; the caller decides what to do with it (RNF09).
18	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({
19	    required String content,
20	    required EntrySource source,
21	    int? mediaDurationSeconds,
22	  });
23	
24	  /// Calls `entries-list` (`ApiClient.get`, via
25	  /// `EntriesRemoteDataSource`), newest-first by `occurredAt` — server
26	  /// behavior assumed, undocumented (Code Map, decided per AGENTS.md
27	  /// policy: "where `docs/input/` is silent... decide and proceed").
28	  ///
29	  /// On [Failure.networkOffline]/[Failure.networkTimeout] specifically,
30	  /// falls back to a full dump of the `entries` Hive box, sorted
31	  /// `occurredAt` desc, with `EntriesPage.nextCursor: null` (Boundaries) —
32	  /// every *other* [Failure] (e.g. [Failure.authExpired]) propagates as
33	  /// `Left`, unmapped (RNF09).
34	  ///
35	  /// A successful page persists every item to the `entries` Hive box
36	  /// *before* returning `Right` — same "persist then return" ordering
37	  /// [create] already uses.
38	  Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({String? cursor, int limit = 20});
39	
40	  /// spec-4-4 (RF07) — calls `entries-get` (`ApiClient.get`, via
41	  /// `EntriesRemoteDataSource`) with [id] as the one path parameter, then
42	  /// persists the fetched entry to the `entries` Hive box (`put`) *before*
43	  /// returning `Right` — same "persist then return" ordering
44	  /// [create]/[list] already use. AD-11 keeps this port create+read-only,
45	  /// not count-capped — [search] (spec-5-1) added a fourth method without
46	  /// contradicting that.
47	  ///
48	  /// On [Failure.networkOffline]/[Failure.networkTimeout] specifically,
49	  /// falls back to `entriesBox.get(id)` if present; a cache miss propagates
50	  /// the original failure unchanged (no synthesized not-found — that
51	  /// distinction belongs to whichever `Failure` the backend/network
52	  /// actually produced). Every *other* [Failure] — including
53	  /// [Failure.notFound] for an id that never existed or belongs to another
54	  /// user — is returned as `Left`, unmapped (RNF09); RNF04 (identical
55	  /// treatment for both causes) is the caller's own rendering job, never
56	  /// this repository's.
57	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id);
58	
59	  /// spec-5-1 — calls `entries-search` (`ApiClient.get`, via
60	  /// `EntriesRemoteDataSource`) with [query] as the one `q` query
61	  /// parameter (no `limit`/`cursor` — Boundaries). [query] is always
62	  /// already a non-empty, pre-trimmed string by the time it reaches this
63	  /// method — `EntriesSearchCubit` owns that guarantee, never this
64	  /// repository.
65	  ///
66	  /// On success, persists every returned entry to the `entries` Hive box
67	  /// (`putAll`) *before* returning `Right` — same "persist then return"
68	  /// ordering [list]/[getById] already use. Unlike [list]/[getById], there
69	  /// is no offline/timeout cache fallback here (AD-9: no client-side
70	  /// vector index) — every [Failure], including
71	  /// [Failure.networkOffline], is returned as `Left`, unmapped (RNF09).
72	  Future<Either<Failure, List<Entry>>> search(String query);
73	}

1	/// `POST /entries`'s four possible origins (`openapi.yaml:345-351`). This
2	/// story only ever produces [manual] (Boundaries: "source=manual for this
3	/// story") — the other three exist here already so the port
4	/// ([EntriesRepository.create]) doesn't need to change shape when Stories
5	/// 3.2/3.3 (audio/photo) and RF10 (chat) start passing them.
6	enum EntrySource { manual, audio, photo, chat }
7	
8	/// A saved journal entry — plain `{id, content, source, chatMessageId,
9	/// occurredAt, serverRevision, createdAt, updatedAt, mediaDurationSeconds}`
10	/// class, no `freezed` (mirrors `AuthenticatedUser`: this feature has no
11	/// need for the union/copyWith machinery `Failure` uses). Boundaries:
12	/// never a field beyond this exact set — `tags`/`piiStatus`/`piiSpans`/
13	/// `embeddingStatus` still belong to later epics, not this story.
14	/// [mediaDurationSeconds] was the one field Story 3.1 deferred (its own
15	/// comment named it "later epics") — spec-3-2 is that story, for the
16	/// `source: audio` entries it produces.
17	///
18	/// [occurredAt]/[createdAt]/[updatedAt] are kept as the backend's own ISO
19	/// 8601 strings rather than parsed into `DateTime` on this entity itself —
20	/// spec-4-1's `groupEntriesByDate()`/`EntryRecordCard`'s own time label
21	/// each parse [occurredAt] at their own call site instead, so a malformed
22	/// string only ever risks throwing at the one place that actually needs
23	/// the parsed value, never here.
24	class Entry {
25	  const Entry({
26	    required this.id,
27	    required this.content,
28	    required this.source,
29	    required this.chatMessageId,
30	    required this.occurredAt,
31	    required this.serverRevision,
32	    required this.createdAt,
33	    required this.updatedAt,
34	    this.mediaDurationSeconds,
35	  });
36	
37	  final String id;
38	  final String content;
39	  final EntrySource source;
40	
41	  /// Non-null only for a [EntrySource.chat]-sourced entry (RF10) — always
42	  /// `null` for this story's [EntrySource.manual] entries.
43	  final String? chatMessageId;
44	  final String occurredAt;
45	  final int serverRevision;
46	  final String createdAt;
47	  final String updatedAt;
48	
49	  /// Non-null only for an [EntrySource.audio]-sourced entry
50	  /// (`AudioEntryCubit.save()`) — `null` for every other source.
51	  final int? mediaDurationSeconds;
52	
53	  @override
54	  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
55	      identical(this, other) ||
56	      (other is Entry &&
57	          other.id == id &&
58	          other.content == content &&
59	          other.source == source &&
60	          other.chatMessageId == chatMessageId &&
61	          other.occurredAt == occurredAt &&
62	          other.serverRevision == serverRevision &&
63	          other.createdAt == createdAt &&
64	          other.updatedAt == updatedAt &&
65	          other.mediaDurationSeconds == mediaDurationSeconds);
66	
67	  @override
68	  int get hashCode => Object.hash(
69	    id,
70	    content,
71	    source,
72	    chatMessageId,
73	    occurredAt,
74	    serverRevision,
75	    createdAt,
76	    updatedAt,
77	    mediaDurationSeconds,
78	  );
79	
80	  @override
81	  String toString() =>
82	      'Entry(id: $id, content: $content, source: $source, '
83	      'chatMessageId: $chatMessageId, occurredAt: $occurredAt, '
84	      'serverRevision: $serverRevision, createdAt: $createdAt, '
85	      'updatedAt: $updatedAt, '
86	      'mediaDurationSeconds: $mediaDurationSeconds)';
87	}

44:### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
45-Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).
46-
47-**Acceptance criteria:**
48-- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
49-- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
50-- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
51-- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
52-- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

55-A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

58-- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.

# Epic 5 Context: Semantic Search & Filtering

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Users can find any Entry again by meaning rather than exact keyword match, and narrow results by source and date range, with search input debounced and filter-clearing restoring the full list without a reload. This epic realizes journey UJ-4 (finding a past entry by meaning, then narrowing with filters) and depends on Epic 4's timeline screen (Meus Registros) as the surface search and filtering mount onto. It extends the same `EntriesRepository` port Epic 3 introduced with `list`/`search` capabilities — it introduces no second Entry model — but stands as its own epic because it is its own user-facing milestone, not a structural completion of Epic 4's job.

## Stories

- Story 5.1: Semantic Search with Debounced Input
- Story 5.2: Metadata Filters
- Story 5.3: Combined Search + Filter & Non-Disruptive Clearing

## Requirements & Constraints

- Search is meaning-based, not literal: a query for one word must surface entries that only use a semantically related word, never requiring exact text match.
- Search input is debounced 300ms client-side before any request fires — the backend performs no throttling of its own, so the debounce is entirely the app's responsibility.
- Filtering is limited to source (manual/audio/photo/chat) and date range (`dateFrom`/`dateTo`) only. There is no tag/category filter anywhere — tags exist only as a read-only, embedded field on an Entry (populated by seed data, never user-created or filterable).
- Filtering with no active search term queries the plain entries-list; filtering combined with an active search term queries the semantic-search endpoint, carrying the same filter parameters. Multiple simultaneous filters (and a search term, when present) combine with AND semantics only — never OR.
- Clearing active filters restores the full unfiltered list in place, without a full screen reload or re-mount.
- The app is cloud-only: offline permits viewing already-cached entries but never writing. After a reconnect, the local cache must stay duplicate-free — no entry appears twice.
- A loading indicator appears only once a request exceeds ~300ms; faster responses show no loading UI at all.

## Technical Decisions

- Call the backend only via its function name, never the literal REST path: entries-list at `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/entries-list` (used for `GET /entries` with `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`/`cursor`/`limit`) and entries-search at `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/entries-search` (used for `GET /entries/search` with `q`/`source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`/`limit`, capped at 50). Note entries-search has **no** `cursor` parameter — unlike entries-list, it is not paginated.
- Extend the existing `EntriesRepository` port (owned by `entries/domain`, introduced in Epic 3) with `list` and `search` methods; the port still exposes create and read only in spirit — no update/delete is ever added, and no second Entry model is created for search results.
- Offline carve-out: semantic search has no client-side vector index, so a search attempted offline resolves immediately to `Failure.networkOffline`, exactly like a write — it is never served from the local cache. Plain filtered list reads, by contrast, may still fall back to the cached Hive box.
- Every query dimension (source, date range, the search term itself) must be a server-side query parameter; the Hive box continues to store exactly what the server returned, keyed by id — no local filtering, joining, sorting, or re-deriving of the cached collection is ever implemented client-side.
- Screens in this epic that are single-data-source, single-fetch-lifecycle use the shared generic `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) state wrapper from `core/`, rather than defining a feature-specific sealed state class.
- Repository methods still return `Either<Failure, T>`, consistent with the rest of the app's resilience contract.

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Search bar: paper-elevated input with a trailing funnel icon, permanently docked at the top of Meus Registros; it is never submitted via a button — only the debounced live query matters.
- Filter chips: sage background, dark-olive text, fully rounded. Single-choice (date range) and multi-choice (source) filters look visually identical and differ only in underlying behavior.
- Filter sheet: a `radiusLg`/`elevation2` bottom sheet with filter groups labeled in the mono-caption text style.
- Representative flow from the design walkthrough: a user searches "ansiedade" and sees results that only mention a related word ("nervosismo"); she then opens the filter sheet and narrows to a date range plus the audio source, and results re-narrow with AND logic.
- Entrance choreography is limited to the two system-wide animations (`sheetUp` for the bottom sheet, `scrimIn` for any scrim) — no other motion is introduced.
- Filter chips and the search/filter surfaces are a tight-fit area for Dynamic Type — verify text does not truncate or clip at the largest accessibility size.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Depends on Epic 4: search and filtering operate over the Meus Registros timeline screen and the entries Hive cache Epic 4 already built; there is nothing to search or filter before that exists.
- Depends on Epic 3's `EntriesRepository` port (introduced under `entries/domain`) being extended here rather than replaced — Story 5.1/5.2 add `search`/`list` capabilities to that one existing port.
- Story 5.3 depends on both 5.1 (search) and 5.2 (filters) being in place, since it is specifically the combined-query and clearing behavior layered on top of both.

Implemented spec-5-2-metadata-filters.md in full. `fvm flutter analyze` → zero issues; `fvm flutter test` → 794/794 passing (up from 784 baseline; +10 new tests added beyond the baseline count, since several existing files also gained new test cases).

## What changed

**Domain/data (filter plumbing, AND-logic at the server):**
- `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` — `list()` gains `EntrySource? source, DateTime? dateFrom, DateTime? dateTo`.
- `lib/features/entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` — `list()` forwards `source.name`/`dateFrom.toIso8601String()`/`dateTo.toIso8601String()` as `entries-list` query params, each omitted when null (same `?x` convention as the existing `cursor`/`mediaDurationSeconds` handling).

message.content:
The coordinator sent a message while you were working:
Code review of your spec-5-2 implementation surfaced 8 confirmed, mechanically-fixable findings. Apply all 8 as patches directly on the same working tree (no need to re-read the whole spec). After applying, re-run `fvm flutter analyze` (expect zero issues) and `fvm flutter test` (expect all passing) and report back.

1. **Timezone-naive date filters sent to the backend** — `lib/features/entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart:73-74` sends `dateFrom`/`dateTo` via `.toIso8601String()` on local (non-UTC) `DateTime`s. A local-time `DateTime.toIso8601String()` has no `Z`/offset suffix, which is non-compliant with the OpenAPI contract's `format: date-time` (RFC3339, which requires an explicit offset). Fix: call `.toUtc()` before `.toIso8601String()` (either in `EntriesFilterSheet`'s `DateRangePreset.rangeFrom()` when constructing the bounds, or in the remote data source just before serializing — pick whichever keeps the existing local-time semantics of "local midnight this Monday" etc. correct, i.e. convert to UTC only at the serialization boundary, not when computing the local calendar bounds).

2. **A newly-created entry bypasses the active filter** — `lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit.dart`'s `_onPendingWritesChanged`/`_onEntryConfirmed` (~lines 85-153) unconditionally prepend the new/pending entry into `MeusRegistrosLoaded.entries`, with no check against `_activeSource`/`_activeDateFrom`/`_activeDateTo`. If a user has `source: audio` active and saves a new manual-text entry, that entry now visibly violates the active filter. Fix: before prepending/showing the placeholder in both handlers, check whether the entry/pending-write matches the currently active filter (source equality; occurredAt within `[_activeDateFrom, _activeDateTo]` when set) and skip the prepend when it doesn't match.

3. **The funnel "filled" (active-filters) indicator shows during unrelated search results** — `lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:208` passes `hasActiveFilters: widget.cubit.hasActiveFilters` to `EntriesSearchBar` unconditionally, regardless of `EntriesSearchCubit`'s state. A user with filters active who starts a search sees the funnel still "filled" next to search results that were never filtered (filters+search integration is 5.3's job, scoped out of 5.2). Fix: gate the filled indicator so it only shows `true` when `searchState is ResourceIdle<List<Entry>>` (i.e. the plain/filtered timeline is what's actually on screen) — `false` otherwise.

4. **The error-state retry button silently drops active filters** — `lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:233` wires `onRetry: widget.cubit.loadFirstPage`, but `loadFirstPage()` resets `_activeSource`/`_activeDateFrom`/`_activeDateTo` to null before reloading (by design, for the fresh-mount case). So retrying a failed *filtered* query silently succeeds with the full unfiltered list instead of retrying the same filtered query. Fix: add a method on `MeusRegistrosCubit` that retries with the currently-active filters intact (e.g. `retryCurrentPage()` calling the same internal `_loadFiltered()` body without resetting `_activeSource`/`_activeDateFrom`/`_activeDateTo`), and wire `onRetry` to that instead of `loadFirstPage`.

5. **`dateRangePresetMatching` has a real ordering bug plus a staleness issue** — `lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet.dart`'s `dateRangePresetMatching()` checks `thisWeek` before `thisMonth`. When the month's 1st day is also this week's Monday, `thisWeek`'s check matches first, so a month-long filter re-opens mislabeled as "Esta semana". Separately, re-deriving the preset by exact-equality against boundaries computed fresh from `DateTime.now()` at reopen time means a filter applied just before a day/week/month rolls over no longer matches any preset once that boundary passes, silently falling back to "Todo o período" in the sheet/chip label even though the filter is still actually active. Fix: check `thisMonth` before `thisWeek` to resolve the ordering bug; if you want to also fix the staleness issue, consider storing which preset was actually selected (not just the derived `dateFrom`) so reopening doesn't depend on re-deriving it from a moving "now" — but if that's a bigger change than you're comfortable making as a patch, the ordering fix alone is the required minimum.

6. **No Dynamic Type / accessibility-scaling test for the new `EntriesFilterSheet`** — the widget's own doc comment cites epic-5-context.md's "tight-fit area for Dynamic Type — verify text does not truncate or clip at the largest accessibility size" note and justifies its `SingleChildScrollView` wrapper specifically on that basis, but `test/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet_test.dart` has no test setting a large `TextScaler`/`textScaleFactor` to verify the guard actually works. Add one.

7. **No screen-level widget test exercises two active-filter chips rendered together, or the date-range chip's own "x"** — `test/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen_test.dart`'s `spec-5-2` group only ever selects a *source* chip before tapping "Aplicar"; none of its tests select a date-range preset too, so `_ActiveFiltersRow`'s `hasDateRange` branch and the date-range chip's distinct `onRemove` (which must drop the date range while keeping `source`) are never exercised at the screen/widget level — only indirectly at the cubit level. Add a test: open the sheet, select a source chip AND a date-range preset (e.g. "Áudio" + "Este mês"), tap "Aplicar", assert both chips render, then tap the date-range chip's own "x" and assert the next `list()` call keeps `source: EntrySource.audio` while `dateFrom`/`dateTo` go back to `null`.

8. **`EntriesFilterSheet.show()`'s reduce-motion branch is untested** — it copies `InsertionModal.show()`'s reduce-motion-aware entrance/exit handling (`disableAnimations` → `Duration.zero`), but unlike `InsertionModal` (which has a dedicated reduce-motion test), nothing sets `MediaQuery.disableAnimations`/`AccessibilityFeatures` before opening the filter sheet in any test. Add one, following `insertion_modal_test.dart`'s existing reduce-motion test pattern.

Three other findings from review were considered and rejected as not actionable (for your awareness, no action needed): offline+filters silently showing the unfiltered cache is an explicit, already-frozen spec decision (AD-9), not a bug; the funnel button staying tappable during an active search is inert by design (updates hidden cubit state with no visible effect until search clears) and not incorrect; and "date-range boundary inclusivity" isn't testable client-side since the app only forwards `dateFrom`/`dateTo` verbatim — inclusivity is the backend's own contract behavior.

Address this before completing your current task.

input.message:
Applied all 8 code-review findings as patches on the same working tree. `fvm flutter analyze` → zero issues. `fvm flutter test` → 808/808 passing (up from 794; added 14 new tests, replaced 1 existing assertion).

## Fixes applied

1. **Timezone-naive dates** — `entries_remote_data_source.dart`: `dateFrom`/`dateTo` now serialize via `.toUtc().toIso8601String()` (was plain `.toIso8601String()` on local time, which omits the `Z`/offset RFC3339 requires). Conversion happens only at this serialization boundary, so `EntriesFilterSheet`'s local-calendar computations ("this Monday", "the 1st of this month") are untouched. Updated the two existing data-source tests to assert against `.toUtc().toIso8601String()` and added an explicit `endsWith('Z')` check.

2. **New entry/pending write bypassing the active filter** — `meus_registros_cubit.dart`: added `_matchesActiveFilters({source, occurredAt})` and a `_visiblePendingWrites` getter (the full `_pendingWrites` filtered through it). `_onEntryConfirmed` now only prepends a confirmed entry into `entries` when it matches the active filter (otherwise the Loaded state's entries are left untouched, and an Empty/Error state stays as-is rather than spuriously transitioning). `_onPendingWritesChanged` and both `_loadFiltered()` emit sites now attach `_visiblePendingWrites` instead of the raw list, so a non-matching pending write's placeholder card never renders. Added 7 cubit tests (matching + non-matching confirmed entry, matching + non-matching pending write, source filter, date-range filter, and the "already-outstanding-before-first-load" ordering case).

3. **Funnel icon "filled" during unrelated search results** — `meus_registros_screen.dart`: the search bar's host `Padding` now nests `BlocBuilder<EntriesSearchCubit,...>` around the existing `BlocBuilder<MeusRegistrosCubit,...>`; `hasActiveFilters` is now `searchState is ResourceIdle<List<Entry>> && widget.cubit.hasActiveFilters`. Added a screen-level regression test: apply a filter (funnel fills), type a query (funnel reverts to muted while search results show), clear the query (funnel fills again).

4. **Error-state retry dropping active filters** — `meus_registros_cubit.dart`: added `retryCurrentPage()` (delegates straight to the existing `_loadFiltered()`, unlike `loadFirstPage()` which resets the filter selection first). Screen's `_ErrorState.onRetry` now wired to `retryCurrentPage` instead of `loadFirstPage`. Added a cubit test proving a retry after a filtered failure still carries the same `source`.

5. **`dateRangePresetMatching` ordering bug** — `entries_filter_sheet.dart`: swapped the check order so `thisMonth` is tested before `thisWeek` (the required minimum fix; left the separate "staleness vs. a moving `now`" issue as a known, documented limitation, per the review's own explicit allowance). Added a deterministic unit test that finds a real month-start-that's-also-a-Monday collision date and asserts it now resolves to `thisMonth`, plus a control test for the ordinary non-colliding `thisWeek` case.

6. **No Dynamic Type test for `EntriesFilterSheet`** — added a `textScaler` param to the test file's `_pumpSheet` helper and a new test at `TextScaler.linear(3.0)` asserting `tester.takeException()` is null and the sheet still renders (validates the `SingleChildScrollView` guard the widget's own doc already cited).

7. **No screen-level test for two simultaneous chips / the date-range chip's own "x"** — added a `meus_registros_screen_test.dart` test: select "Áudio" + "Este mês" together, Aplicar, assert both chips render and the query carries both; tap the *second* (date-range) chip's "x"; assert the next `list()` call keeps `source: EntrySource.audio` while `dateFrom`/`dateTo` go back to `null`.

8. **Reduce-motion path untested for `EntriesFilterSheet.show()`** — added `_openSheet()` to the filter-sheet test file, mirroring `insertion_modal_test.dart`'s `_openModal` pattern exactly (button host + `MediaQuery.copyWith(disableAnimations: true)`), and a test asserting the sheet is fully rendered after a single `pump()` (no mid-transition frame).

No other files touched. The three findings the coordinator flagged as rejected (offline+filters per AD-9, funnel tappable during search, date-boundary inclusivity) were left as-is, no action taken.
